newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rejects U.S. criticism on auto trade.
newsitem.headline: Japan rejects U.S. criticism on auto trade.

text.p: Japan Tuesday rejected U.S. charges that it had "stalled" on deregulation in its automotive market and said Tokyo's widening surplus in the sector was a temporary blip.
"We are sincerely and fully implementing the agreement," a Japanese trade official told Reuters. "We hope for more effort on the U.S. (carmakers') side."

U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Monday that Japan had stalled on deregulation of its automotive market. "That is of significant concern and inexcusable," Barshefsky told Reuters in an interview. "There is no question that the number of vehicle dealerships is also not adequate."

A 1995 U.S.-Japan trade agreement, reached after bitter talks that took the two nations to the brink of a trade war, called on Tokyo to give foreign car and car parts suppliers more access and encourage more dealers to sell U.S. cars.

The pact allowed both sides to claim victory in the dispute but sowed the seeds for future disagreement by allowing Washington to calculate numerical "expectations" for progress while letting Tokyo refrain from promising to meet any targets.

Since the deal was struck, the U.S. deficit in the auto sector has risen to 66 percent of the overall U.S. deficit with Japan from 60 percent two years ago. "The numbers are disturbing," Barshefsky said.

A weaker yen helped boost Japanese car exports to the United States by 22.3 percent in the January-June period from a year earlier, the first such increase since the first half of 1986, according to figures released on Monday.
U.S. officials have warned Tokyo not to export its way out of its economic woes and let its trade surplus get out of hand.
Trade Minister Shinji Sato told a news conference on Tuesday that the recent rise in Japan's surplus was temporary, but acknowledged trade tempers could fray if the gap failed to narrow in the fall.
"I believe that it is a temporary problem, although I realise that if the trade surplus does not come down in the autumn, it will be a tough situation," Sato said.

Japanese car exports to the United States are now half the level they were five years ago because of increased output by Japanese carmakers in America and that trend will continue, the Japanese trade official said.
